sources.entry: Tickeys - Instant audio feedback for typing. macOS version.

summary.one_liner: Tickeys is a macOS app that plays instant sound effects as you type, written in Rust as a learning demo.
summary.what_it_does: Tickeys plays short audio clips on each keystroke to give typing audible feedback. It ships with built-in sound schemes that map sounds to keys, with special sounds for space, backspace and enter. Users can add custom schemes by copying an existing effect directory, renaming it, and editing a schemes.json file that lists sound files and key-to-sound mappings by keyCode. Sounds are WAV files replaced or added inside the app bundle's data directory. The README describes the project as a demo for learning Rust. Versions for Linux and Windows are linked from the README as separate projects or downloads.
use_cases: add typing sound effects on mac
learn rust with a desktop app example
install typing sounds via homebrew cask
how_to_run: Or download the dmg from the releases page and install it
To add a custom scheme: copy an effect directory under Tickeys.app/Contents/Resources/data/ and rename it
Edit schemes.json: add an entry with matching name, display_name, files, non_unique_count and key_audio_map
Add or replace the .wav files, save the JSON, then re-launch Tickeys
For development: brew install freealut openssl
notable: Customizable sound schemes defined in schemes.json with per-key sound mapping by keyCode
Built-in effects with separate sounds for space, backspace and enter keys
Written in Rust and described as a demo for learning Rust
Sibling versions exist for Linux and Windows
caveats: Development build requires alut and openssl libraries installed via Homebrew
Only the macOS version is covered by this repository's README; other platforms are linked separately
README is brief and gives no detailed documentation on the scheme format beyond the example
